Each divisor set T(g,d) is an integer count by Möbius inversion of A(e,d), so three rank formulas partition all choices. Exact cyclotomic direct enumeration checks all minors for cyclic orders 3,4,5,6,7,8,9,10,12,15,16,18; enumeration is auxiliary to the general proof.

originality.rationale: Best-knowledge originality resides in all-modulus rank 1,2,3 census via a uniform Möbius divisor formula and the rank-one factorization criterion, not the previously known prime-power, p-square, 2p, principal, or Hadamard cases. Primary full-text and indexed claims were compared for logical coverage, not keywords.
residual_risks: An older result using gcd of index differences, Fourier primitive sets or divisor-lattice language might state the same unrestricted classification under a different name.

value.rationale: Arbitrary cyclic Fourier three-by-three submatrix ranks are a natural finite harmonic sampling invariant. The complete all-N classification counts each rank without brute-force minors, reveals when rank-one collapse occurs at squarefree composite orders despite nonsingular principal minors, and handles mixed-prime-power arithmetic not described by prior restricted families.
